svg.text: Walk 5 - the data plane, case by case

Three cases, each three stitched tunnel legs, source on the left (site B) → destination on the right (site A) | numbered badges match the numbered steps | outer addresses are VTEP loopbacks (Lo1) - Lo0 is peering only, never in a packet header
A - First packet: ARP broadcast (BUM, VNI 1010)

g.text: 1. R_VPC1 broadcasts who-has 192.168.10.10; Leaf31 floods per its VNI 1010 HER list - one copy, to 10.255.31.101 (no site A VTEP is in the list). Outer: 10.255.31.113 → 10.255.31.101.

2. Border2 decapsulates, floods its local VLAN 10 (empty), and re-encapsulates one copy per its interconnect IMET list. Outer: 10.255.31.101 → 10.255.255.101. Split horizon: nothing returns toward Leaf31.
3. Border1 decapsulates and head-end-replicates into site A's flood list: copies to .112 and .113 - and nothing back toward the DCI, the domain the frame arrived from.
4. One MLAG member wins the .112 copy (section 2.4's rules) and floods VLAN 10; VPC1 answers, and the unicast reply rides the same three legs in reverse.

svg.text: B - Steady state: known unicast, R_VPC1 → VPC1 (VNI 1010)

g.text: 1. Leaf31's MAC table: VPC1-MAC → VTEP 10.255.31.101 (installed from Walk 4's re-originated Type-2). Encapsulate: outer 10.255.31.113 → 10.255.31.101, routed Leaf31 → SP31 → Border2.
2. Border2 decapsulates; its MAC table says VPC1-MAC → VTEP 10.255.255.101. Re-encapsulate: outer 10.255.31.101 → 10.255.255.101, routed Border2 → DCI → Border1.
3. Border1 decapsulates; VPC1-MAC → VTEP 10.255.255.112. Re-encapsulate: outer 10.255.255.101 → 10.255.255.112, either spine, either MLAG member decapsulates and bridges to VPC1.
The inner Ethernet frame is untouched end to end - only the outer header is rewritten at each stitch point.

svg.text: C - Routed: R_VPC1 → VPC3, VLAN 30 never stretched (symmetric IRB, VNI 50000)

g.text: 1. Leaf31, VRF TENANT_A: 192.168.30.0/24 → VTEP 10.255.31.101, router MAC = Border2's (Walk 4's RMAC row). Route into VNI 50000: inner DMAC = Border2's RMAC, outer 10.255.31.113 → 10.255.31.101.
2. Border2 decapsulates and routes again in its own VRF TENANT_A: prefix → 10.255.255.101, RMAC = Border1's. Re-encapsulate in VNI 50000 across the DCI.
3. Border1 decapsulates and routes a third time: prefix → .112 or .113 (ECMP - all three site A leaves originate VLAN 30). Inner DMAC = the chosen leaf's RMAC.
4. The landing leaf routes from VNI 50000 into VLAN 30 and delivers to VPC3. Routed at every hop: inner MACs rewritten each leg, inner IPs constant end to end.
Three independent VXLAN tunnel legs, one per domain - each converges, ECMPs, and fails in its own underlay; the DCI carries only gateway-to-gateway packets (+50 B headroom per leg)
Every leg's endpoints come from Walk 4's re-originated routes: no device ever needs a route to a VTEP outside its own domain
Cases A and B bridge - the inner frame is constant. Case C routes - a VRF lookup at the head of every leg, RMAC chain Border2 → Border1 → leaf. Both gateways must carry VRF TENANT_A + VNI 50000
Case A's copy count across the DCI is one, always - Border1 does site A's fan-out locally (the 6.2 design sent one copy per site A VTEP)
